response.text:
I quickly followed suit, and descending into the bar-room accosted the grinning landlord very pleasantly. I cherished no malice towards him, though he had been skylarking with me not a little in the matter of my bedfellow. A good laugh is a mighty good thing, and rather too scarce a good thing; the more’s the pity. So, if any one man, in his own proper person, afford stuff for a good joke to anybody, let him not be backward, but let him cheerfully allow himself to spend and be spent in that way. And the man that has anything bountifully laughable about him, be sure there is more in that man than you perhaps think for.

The bar-room was now full of the boarders from the night before—nearly all whalemen: mates, sea carpenters, coopers, blacksmiths, harpooneers, and ship keepers; a brown and brawny company with bosky beards, an unshorn set in monkey jackets for morning gowns.

This young fellow’s healthy cheek is like a sun-toasted pear in hue; he cannot have been three days landed from his Indian voyage. But who could show a cheek like Queequeg? which, barred with various tints, seemed like the Andes’ western slope, to show forth in one array contrasting climates, zone by zone.

They say that men who have seen the world thereby become quite at ease in manner. Not always: Ledyard, the great New England traveller, and Mungo Park, the Scotch one—of all men, they possessed the least assurance in the parlor. But perhaps the mere crossing of Siberia in a sledge drawn by dogs, or taking a long solitary walk on an empty stomach in the negro heart of Africa—this kind of travel, I say, may not be the very best mode of attaining a high social polish. Still, for the most part, that sort of thing is to be had anywhere. After we were all seated at the table, to my no small surprise nearly every man maintained a profound silence—these sea-dogs, many of whom had boarded great whales on the high seas and duelled them dead without winking; here they sat at a social breakfast table—all of the same calling, all of kindred tastes—looking round as sheepishly at each other as though they had never been out of sight of some sheepfold among the Green Mountains. A curious sight; these bashful bears, these timid warrior whalemen!

But as for Queequeg—why, Queequeg sat there among them, at the head of the table, as cool as an icicle—reaching over it with his harpoon, to the imminent jeopardy of heads, grappling the beefsteaks towards him. Every one knows that in most people’s estimation, to do anything coolly is to do it genteelly.

When breakfast was over he withdrew into the public room, lighted his tomahawk-pipe, and sat there quietly digesting and smoking with his inseparable hat on, while I sallied out for a stroll.
